source.market_name: Kim Jong Un out as Supreme Leader of North Korea by December 31, 2026?

market_name: Kim Jong Un out as Supreme Leader of North Korea by December 31, 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the Polymarket probability move is corroborated by any newswire (Yonhap, Reuters, KCNA) or is isolated; confirm EWY/KRW moving in sympathy.
time_plan.1h: Compare EWY move vs broad EM (EEM) to isolate Korea-specific risk premium; watch USD/KRW offshore.
time_plan.2h: Reassess whether the market spike holds or mean-reverts; look for official denial from Pyongyang which would unwind the move.
time_plan.6h: Check Seoul futures/overnight KOSPI indications and defense-sector reaction; gauge whether move is durable.
time_plan.12h: Evaluate whether EWY has repriced a persistent risk premium or recovered; close out thesis if no corroborating news emerged.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp jump in the implied probability that Kim Jong Un ceases to be Supreme Leader would most plausibly reflect leaked signs of leadership instability, incapacitation, or a succession/regime event in North Korea. Such an event raises acute geopolitical tail risk directly on South Korea's border, triggering risk-off selling of the most liquid foreign proxy for Korean equities (EWY), especially via US-listed ADR/ETF flows when Seoul is closed.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm whether a genuine news catalyst accompanies the probability move; check gold spot and GLD reaction vs DXY.
time_plan.1h: Separate gold's geopolitical bid from rates/USD moves; watch Treasuries for corroborating flight-to-safety.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether the safe-haven bid persists or fades as details clarify.
time_plan.6h: Re-check gold vs equities to confirm risk-off regime still intact.
time_plan.12h: Determine if gold held a geopolitical premium or reverted; close thesis absent confirmation.

predictions.reasoning: An abrupt rise in the probability of a North Korean leadership change implies elevated geopolitical uncertainty, which typically bids safe-haven assets. Gold is the most liquid, broadly-traded hedge and tends to catch a modest flight-to-safety bid during Korean peninsula shocks, though the effect is usually smaller and noisier than the equity risk-off reaction.

evidence_used: Market question concerns removal/incapacitation of Kim Jong Un as North Korean Supreme Leader by end-2026
Resolution triggers on announcement, detention, or effective removal
North Korea leadership instability is a known tail risk for South Korean assets and regional safe havens
uncertainty_notes: The market window runs through end-2026, so a probability move need not imply an imminent 12h event
A probability drift could reflect speculative repositioning rather than leaked information
South Korean markets may be closed during the window, muting direct price discovery and concentrating reaction in US-listed proxies

llm_justification.summary: A sharp rise in the implied probability of Kim Jong Un losing power would most plausibly signal leaked North Korean leadership instability, a classic geopolitical tail risk for the Korean peninsula. The cleanest liquid expressions are risk-off in South Korean equities (EWY down) and a modest safe-haven bid in gold (GLD up). Both mappings are moderate-confidence at best: the market resolves anytime through 2026, so without a corroborating news catalyst a probability move is noise, and the equity reaction only clears the 700bps tradable bar in a genuine acute-event scenario.
key_assumptions: A sharp probability spike reflects real new information about leadership instability, not speculative churn
EWY and GLD remain liquid and tradable during the window
Markets would interpret a Kim removal as destabilizing (raising escalation risk) rather than as a de-escalation
failure_modes: The probability move is pure speculation or a thin-market artifact with no underlying event, so proxies do not move
News is already public and priced, so no fresh asset reaction occurs
A leadership change could be read as de-escalatory, reversing the risk-off direction
EWY is a broad Korea proxy whose moves are dominated by semis/global tech beta, diluting the NK-specific signal
The 2026 horizon means even a correct probability shift may not produce a 12h asset move
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
